## One global grid, sliced per block (YAML `geometry`) {#sec-ch03-globalgrid}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy, code_pin.yml)
sources: src/coord/coordinate.cpp, src/coord/coordinate.hpp, tests/test_coordinate.cpp
status: draft
-->

snapy builds the face coordinates of a block by slicing one global array per axis rather than by spacing the block's
own interval. Spacing per block produces the same physical face from different floating-point arithmetic in the two
blocks that share it and in different decompositions of one problem, and every metric term (areas, volumes, the
spherical-polar and gnomonic source coefficients) inherits that difference. With the slice, a face has one value
whoever owns it, and the cell width is the global $\Delta x_a$ in every block.

Local symbols: $x^{\min}_a, x^{\max}_a$ the declared global bounds of axis $a$ [m or rad];
$n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a$ the declared global cell count of axis $a$ (count); $\Delta x_a$ the global cell width of axis
$a$ [m or rad]; $o_a$ the global index of a block's first interior cell on axis $a$ (count); $X_{a,m}$ entry $m$ of
the global face array of axis $a$; $n_a$ the block's interior cell count on axis $a$ (count);
$x^{\mathrm{blk}}_{a,\min}$ the block's lower bound on axis $a$ [m or rad]; $n_b$ the number of blocks on axis $a$
(count); $b_a$ the block's index along axis $a$, from 0 (count); $n_g$[^rg-e176f04ce147] the ghost cells per side (`nghost`[^rg-6f20f9603219], count);
$q$ the width ratio of a geometric stretched $x_1$ (`x1rat`[^rg-83f2464f46a0], -); $F_k$, $k=0,\dots,n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1$, the interior
faces of a stretched $x_1$; $n_e$ the ghost faces the stretched global array carries per end (count).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Every block's faces are a slice of one global face array per axis (@eq-ch03-globalgrid-slice), so a
face shared by two blocks, or seen under two decompositions, is the same double.

**Data.** In: YAML `geometry: {type, bounds, cells, x1f}` (with `cells/x1rat`) and `distribute: {nb1, nb2, nb3}`.
Out: the block's face positions [m or rad], ghosts included, and its integer offset.

**Placement.** Setup (`repartition`, `reset`).

**Activation.** No switch; always on; a block built without a declared global grid adopts itself as the global grid.
Requires each global count divisible by the blocks on its axis. `geometry/x1f` or `geometry/cells/x1rat` (not both)
makes $x_1$ stretched; default uniform.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact (bitwise) for faces built from the global grid; a mesh generator passed to
`reset_coordinates` rebuilds the faces from the block's own bounds and bypasses the invariant.

**Evidence.** `test_coordinate`, `test_stretched_x1`, `test_deck_x1_wiring`, `test_stretched_x1_ref` (pass at the
pin); `test_cubed_sphere_exchange`, `test_local_horizontal_cells_python`; check `[C16]`.
:::

The scheme is always on. The YAML card declares the global bounds and cell counts; `distribute` declares the number of
blocks per axis; each block's own bounds and counts follow from its place in the layout (@sec-ch03-layouts). A block
built programmatically without a global grid adopts its own bounds and count as the global grid.

The vertical grid and which way is up: $x_1$ is always the vertical axis, a height [m] on a Cartesian grid and the
radius [m] on a spherical-polar or cubed-sphere grid (@sec-appa-conventions). Up is increasing $x_1$: the $x_1$
faces run from `x1min`[^rg-651c23886373] at the bottom to `x1max`[^rg-358e9c8d45a7] at the top, the first interior cell is the lowest, and gravity
pointing down is a negative `grav1`[^rg-a20bd6efce5e] (@sec-ch06-cell). The vertical faces are a slice of one global face array,
evenly spaced by $\Delta x_1$ (@eq-ch03-globalgrid-slice), or stretched when the deck gives `geometry/x1f` or
`geometry/cells/x1rat` (@eq-ch03-globalgrid-x1rat), unless a mesh generator rebuilds them, as derived below.

### Derivation

The scheme is a design invariant, not an approximation, so the derivation is the argument that two blocks agree.
Axis $a$ is declared as $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a$ cells on $[x^{\min}_a, x^{\max}_a]$, with the global width

$$
\Delta x_a = \frac{x^{\max}_a - x^{\min}_a}{n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a}.
$$

The global face array $X_a$ has $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a + 2n_g + 1$ entries spaced over the interval
$[x^{\min}_a - n_g\Delta x_a,\ x^{\max}_a + n_g\Delta x_a]$, so entry $m$ is global face $m - n_g$ and the $n_g$
outermost entries on each side are ghost faces. A block whose first interior cell is global cell $o_a$ and which
holds $n_a$ interior cells takes the consecutive entries

$$
x_{a,\,m} = X_{a,\,o_a + m}, \qquad m = 0, \dots, n_a + 2n_g,
$$ {#eq-ch03-globalgrid-slice}

The slice is `block_faces_` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::block_faces_ >}}). Its offset is the rounded quotient

$$
o_a = \operatorname{round}\!\left(\frac{x^{\mathrm{blk}}_{a,\min} - x^{\min}_a}{\Delta x_a}\right).
$$ {#eq-ch03-globalgrid-offset}

The offset is `_offset` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::_offset >}}), called through `ix1`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateOptionsImpl >}}).

Two blocks that share global face $g$ read the same entry $X_{a,g+n_g}$, so their face values are equal bit for bit,
and the same holds between any two decompositions that slice the same $X_a$. The offset ([-@eq-ch03-globalgrid-offset])
needs rounding, not truncation: `repartition` places block $b_a$ at $x^{\min}_a + b_a\,(x^{\max}_a - x^{\min}_a)/n_b$, so the
quotient is an integer only up to round-off, and truncating a value just below an integer would shift the block by a
whole cell. Nothing is truncated in this scheme; the statement is exact.

The check builds $X_a$ for $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a = 96$ on $[-3, 5]$ with $n_g = 3$, slices it with three pairs of
decompositions and compares every shared entry as a bit pattern: 634 shared entries, no mismatch. It then walks the
block boundaries `repartition` produces for $n_b = 2$ to $24$: rounding recovers the exact integer at all 107 of
them, while truncation is a whole cell low at two, the first being $n_b = 12$, $b_a = 1$, where it gives 7 instead
of 8 (`[C16]`).[^gg-c16]

#### Stretched $x_1$

A deck may replace the evenly spaced $x_1$ faces by its own. `geometry/x1f` is the list of the
$n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1+1$ interior faces $F_0<\dots<F_{n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1}$. `geometry/cells/x1rat` is the width ratio
$q>0$ of a geometric series of faces between the bounds,

$$
F_k = x^{\min}_1+\left(x^{\max}_1-x^{\min}_1\right)\frac{q^k-1}{q^{\,n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1}-1},\qquad
F_{n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1}=x^{\max}_1,
$$ {#eq-ch03-globalgrid-x1rat}

evaluated as `expm1(k ln q)/expm1(n ln q)` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The
widths $F_{k+1}-F_k=(x^{\max}_1-x^{\min}_1)\,q^k(q-1)/(q^{n}-1)$ have the constant ratio $q$, and $q=1$ is the uniform
grid, for which the code keeps the evenly spaced path. Either way the faces become the axis's global faces, and the
global bounds become $F_0$ and $F_{n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1}$.

The ghost faces mirror the interior widths: the global array carries $n_e=\max(n_g,3)+1$ ghost faces at each end,
$F_{-m}=2F_0-F_m$ and $F_{n+m}=2F_n-F_{n-m}$ for $m=1,\dots,n_e$, so ghost cell $-m$ has the width of interior cell
$m-1$ ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::global_x1f >}}). $n_e$ does not depend on $n_g$ below 3,
so the global faces of two decks that differ only in `nghost` are the same (`global_faces_do_not_depend_on_nghost`).
A block is a slice of that array, as in @eq-ch03-globalgrid-slice, starting at the entry of its first face; its offset
is the index of the global face nearest its lower bound, `_face_index`, and the slice must start and end exactly on
global faces (`_resolve_x1_faces`), so two blocks again share every face as one double.

[^gg-c16]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C16]`; a numpy port of `CoordinateImpl::block_faces_` and `CoordinateOptionsImpl::_offset` at the pin,
    CPU[^rg-254534abaa24], double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The face arrays `x1f`, `x2f`, `x3f` hold face positions (points), $n_a + 2n_g + 1$ per axis on a live axis. The ghost
faces are the global array continued past the domain by $n_g$ widths, so a ghost cell has the same width as an
interior cell. An axis with $n_a \le 1$ is degenerate: it has two faces and no ghost layers, taken from the global
array without the ghost extension, so that $x^{\min}_a + n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a\Delta x_a$, which need not round to
$x^{\max}_a$, is never formed. Cell widths on Cartesian and gnomonic grids are the global $\Delta x_a$
(@sec-ch03-cartesian, @sec-ch03-gnomonic); on spherical-polar they are differences of the sliced faces
(@sec-ch03-sphpolar). On a stretched $x_1$ the $x_1$ widths are face differences on every type, the centres are the
face midpoints (spherical-polar: its centroids), and the centre spacings `dx1v` are differences of the midpoints of
the global faces, mirrored ghosts included ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_metrics_ >}}).
The construction runs once, when a block is built; it is not part of any stage.
@fig-ch03-globalgrid-slice shows the slice for two decompositions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-globalgrid-slice
#| fig-cap: "One global face array along $x_2$ with its ghost extension, sliced for two blocks (top) and three blocks (bottom). Ghost faces of each block are hatched; a face shared by two blocks is one entry of the global array, so both blocks hold the same value."
#| fig-alt: "A row of global faces, with the two-block and three-block slices marked under it and their ghost faces hatched."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_globalgrid_slice import make_fig
make_fig()
```

Setup validates the declared grid. When no global grid is declared on an axis (global count 0), the block adopts
itself; otherwise the block must lie inside the global interval within a tolerance of
$16\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}}\max(\lvert x^{\min}_a\rvert, \lvert x^{\max}_a\rvert, \lvert x^{\max}_a - x^{\min}_a\rvert)$, with
$\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}}$[^rg-fbe9686e1f06] the double-precision machine epsilon, and must be exactly $n_a$ global cells: both its ends must sit on
global faces within that tolerance. The tolerance covers the accumulation in `repartition`, which reaches the last
upper bound by adding block widths. A stretched $x_1$ is split into equal cell counts per $x_1$ block, each block's
bounds read off the face list, so there is no accumulation and the $x_1$ ends must match global faces exactly.

: Code map of the global grid. {#tbl-ch03-globalgrid-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-globalgrid-code):

1. `from_yaml` reads `geometry.type` (default `cartesian`), the bounds (default $[0,1]$ on each axis, with `x2min_pi`[^rg-e074f181bf79]
   style keys multiplied by $\pi$) and the cell counts into the global fields
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). Unknown keys are refused by `check_keys`.
   With `x1f` or `cells/x1rat` it builds the interior face list (@eq-ch03-globalgrid-x1rat), checks that it
   increases strictly and that adjacent widths differ by at most `kX1MaxWidthRatio` $=1.5$, and stores it as
   `x1f_interior`, which makes `stretched_x1()` true.
2. A card with `bounds`[^rg-7888cc7a7f34] and no `cells`[^rg-7e4292ba0a15] declares one cell per axis spanning the bounds, and sets the block bounds to
   the same interval: `global_nx1` is set to 1 ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
3. Each global count must be divisible by the blocks on its axis; otherwise setup stops with "Number of total x1
   grids must be divisible by the number of mesh blocks in x1 direction" (and the same for x2, x3), checked with
   `nb1` and its siblings ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
4. `nghost` is read (default 1) and `interp_order`[^rg-5ae45a042270] (default 2); then `repartition` sets the block's bounds from its
   layout location, with $x_1$ forced to the first block on the cubed sphere, and its counts to
   $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a/n_b$ ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::repartition >}}). On a stretched
   $x_1$ the $x_1$ bounds are faces $l_1 n$ and $(l_1+1)n$ of the list, $n=n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1/n_{b}$. After the
   repartition a stretched $x_1$ is checked to have $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1\ge n_e$ and more than one cell per block, and
   each live axis to have at least $n_g$ cells per block.
5. `resolve_global_grid` runs `_resolve_axis` on each axis (`_resolve_x1_faces` for a stretched $x_1$): adopt the
   block when the global count is 0, else
   check inside-ness and the exact cell count ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::_resolve_axis >}}, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::resolve_global_grid >}}). The two refusals a user can hit
   read "block x2 = [...] lies outside the declared global x2 grid" and "... is not exactly n cells of the declared
   global x2 grid".
6. The constructor calls `block_faces_` per axis with the global bounds and count and the block's count and offset
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::CoordinateImpl >}}); `block_faces_` slices the global `linspace`
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::block_faces_ >}}). On a stretched $x_1$ it first refuses any type
   other than `cartesian`, `gnomonic-equiangle` or a spherical-polar grid with $0<x_2^{\min}$, $x_2^{\max}<\pi$, then
   slices `global_x1f` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::global_x1f >}}).
7. Each coordinate type's `reset` then builds widths and centres from these faces (the metric schemes of this
   chapter).

**How to use it.** The global grid is the `geometry` block; the block grid that cuts it is `distribute`
(@sec-ch03-layouts). A two-block slab of 8 by 8 cells:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `x2min`[^rg-f9fe7a2e3627], `x2max`[^rg-6570d7198b2a], `x3min`[^rg-9a187463aabb], `x3max`[^rg-8e0e11089428], `nx1`[^rg-f79ca7158cdc], `nx2`[^rg-34ff2cf5dd50], `nx3`[^rg-c59f0fe092ef], `layout`[^rg-a0f004620ba8], `nb2`[^rg-5502021766c8], `blocks_per_process`[^rg-78b664d1ce43].
```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian                      # the default; spherical-polar, gnomonic-equiangle; cylindrical is a stub
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 1000., x2min: 0., x2max: 1000., x3min: 0., x3max: 1000.}   # x2min_pi etc. times pi
  cells: {nx1: 8, nx2: 8, nx3: 1, nghost: 2}   # interp_order defaults to 2
distribute: {layout: slab, nb2: 2, blocks_per_process: 2}   # nx2 must divide by nb2
```

A stretched $x_1$ of 64 cells whose widths grow by 2% per cell from the bottom wall; the $x_1$ boundaries must be
reflecting:

```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
  bounds: {x1min: 0., x1max: 3.e5, x2min: 0., x2max: 1.e4, x3min: 0., x3max: 1.e4}
  cells: {nx1: 64, nx2: 1, nx3: 1, nghost: 3, x1rat: 1.02}   # or geometry/x1f: [65 faces], not both
```

Two or more blocks in one process are built through `Mesh` (`MeshOptions.from_yaml`); a single `MeshBlock` of a
multi-block layout stops with "MeshBlockImpl: world_size (1) does not match layout partitioning (2)." Refused, each
with its message:

- a key outside `geometry: {type, bounds, cells, x1f}`, `bounds` (the six bounds and the four `_pi` forms) or `cells`
  (`nx1`, `nx2`, `nx3`, `nghost`, `interp_order`, `x1rat`): "unknown key 'geometry/cells/nx4'. Valid keys: nx1, nx2,
  nx3, nghost, interp_order, x1rat.";
- on a stretched $x_1$: both keys ("geometry: give cells/x1rat or x1f, not both"); `x1f` without `cells` ("geometry/x1f
  needs geometry/cells/nx1"); a list of other than $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1+1$ faces; a list whose ends differ from
  `x1min`/`x1max` when those are given; $q\le0$; faces not strictly increasing; adjacent widths differing by more
  than a factor 1.5 ("... outside the stage-1 bound [1/1.5, 1.5]"); $n^{\mathrm{glob}}_1<\max(n_g,3)+1$ or a single
  $x_1$ cell per block; a global count not divisible by the $x_1$ blocks; a geometry other than `cartesian`,
  `gnomonic-equiangle` or a pole-free spherical-polar grid;
- at the first step of a stretched deck ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_check_stretched_x1 >}}): an MPS[^rg-11c0286d8103]
  device, a layout that wraps $x_1$ periodically, and a physical $x_1$ boundary that is not `reflecting` ("a stretched
  x1 ... needs reflecting x1 boundaries: its ghost faces mirror the interior widths");
- a count that does not divide by its blocks: "Number of total x2 grids must be divisible by the number of mesh
  blocks in x2 direction" (the $x_3$ message reads "Number of totla x3 grids …");
- block options that do not sit on the declared grid (programmatic options only; the YAML path computes the block
  bounds itself): "… lies outside the declared global x2 grid" or "… is not exactly n cells of the declared global
  x2 grid".

The keys, the divisibility test and the defaults are these lines of `from_yaml`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}); `repartition` then gives the block
$n_a = n^{\mathrm{glob}}_a/n_b$ cells and its offset $o_a$ of @eq-ch03-globalgrid-offset:

```cpp
  check_keys(node, "geometry", {"type", "bounds", "cells", "x1f"});
  op->type(node["type"].as<std::string>("cartesian"));
    ...
  check_keys(node["cells"], "geometry/cells",
             {"nx1", "nx2", "nx3", "nghost", "interp_order", "x1rat"});
  op->global_nx1() = node["cells"]["nx1"].as<int>(1);
  op->global_nx2() = node["cells"]["nx2"].as<int>(1);
  op->global_nx3() = node["cells"]["nx3"].as<int>(1);
    ...
  int nb1 = playout->options->pz();
  int nb2 = playout->options->px();
  int nb3 = playout->options->py();

  if (op->global_nx1() % nb1 != 0) {
    TORCH_CHECK(
        false,
        "Number of total x1 grids must be divisible by the number of mesh "
        "blocks in x1 direction");
    ...
  op->nghost() = node["cells"]["nghost"].as<int>(1);
    ...
  op->interp_order() = node["cells"]["interp_order"].as<int>(2);
  op->repartition(layout);
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | faces of each block (nb2 = 2, 3) equal the undecomposed faces | bitwise | a shared face is one double |
| `test_coordinate` | programmatic blocks span the caller's bounds | $10^{-15}\Delta x_a$ | round-off of one spacing |
| `test_local_horizontal_cells_python` | the horizontal setter leaves every axis resolved | $10^{-12}\Delta x_a$ | set in the script |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` | gnomonic `x2f`, `dx2f` equal across nb2 = 1, 2, 4 | bitwise | as above |
| `test_stretched_x1` | a face list gives mirrored ghosts and its metrics; `x1rat` gives @eq-ch03-globalgrid-x1rat and `x1rat: 1` the uniform grid; blocks slice the global faces; the global faces do not depend on `nghost`; bad keys and an uneven $x_1$ split are refused | per case, round-off or exact | the construction |
| `test_deck_x1_wiring` | an `x1rat` deck and a face-list deck install the block faces on the $x_1$ reconstruction; a uniform deck installs nothing | exact | contract |
| `test_stretched_x1_ref` | reflecting decks, uniform and stretched, build and step; periodic and outflow $x_1$ and a polar spherical-polar deck are refused | throws or not | contract |

: Tests of the global grid. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-globalgrid-tests}

The bitwise case is `blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateDecomposition.blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise >}}): a six-cell $x_2$ axis is split into two and three blocks and each block's
interior faces are compared with `torch::equal` against the matching slice of the undecomposed grid. The
programmatic cases run from `faces_span_the_callers_bounds_on_every_axis`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.faces_span_the_callers_bounds_on_every_axis >}}) to
`a_declared_block_must_span_exactly_nx_global_faces`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_declared_block_must_span_exactly_nx_global_faces >}});
they cover the adopted grid, the bounds-only card
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_bounds_only_card_keeps_its_declared_domain >}}), a
degenerate axis beside live ones, and the two refusals of step 5
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateProgrammatic.a_block_outside_its_declared_grid_is_refused >}}). The
Python setter test checks the resolved counts and the faces of each axis in `AXES` with `NG` ghost layers
({{< code tests/test_local_horizontal_cells.py AXES >}}, {{< code tests/test_local_horizontal_cells.py NG >}}). The gnomonic case is `subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block >}}).

All entries run on CPU; the gnomonic comparison also has a CUDA[^rg-7dab1148c3f0] case in the same binary, which skips without a
GPU[^rg-326ea2f442e6]. None runs on more than one rank. At the pin `test_coordinate`, `test_stretched_x1` (8 passed),
`test_deck_x1_wiring` (3 passed) and `test_stretched_x1_ref` (18 passed, 4 skipped that need a switch) pass on
CPU;[^gg-run68] `test_cubed_sphere_exchange` and `test_local_horizontal_cells_python` were not run for this chapter
(missing evidence). How far per-block spacing would move the faces is not measured at the pin.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A mesh generator passed to `reset_coordinates` rebuilds the faces from the block's own bounds, outside the
  global-slice invariant ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::reset_coordinates >}}).
- A stretched $x_1$ needs reflecting $x_1$ walls, no periodic $x_1$, no MPS device, a width ratio of adjacent cells
  within 1.5, equal cell counts per $x_1$ block, and one of the three geometries above; each is refused otherwise.
:::

The mesh-generator path is reached only by code that calls `reset_coordinates`; no test at the pin exercises it with
a decomposed grid (not measured). The interpolants the $x_1$ reconstruction accepts on a stretched $x_1$, and their
order there, are those of @sec-ch04; this section covers only the grid. Bitwise decomposition invariance of
the faces is tested for $x_2$ splits of 2 and 3 blocks on Cartesian and of 2 and 4 blocks per panel on the cubed
sphere; $x_1$ and $x_3$ splits of the faces are not tested on their own. The switch combinations that are tested are
listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
